title_en: Interpretations of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Trial of Joint Venture Contract Dispute Cases
keywords_en: contract dispute; court's opinion on trial of joint venture contract disputes
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court Answers to Certain Questions Concerning the Trial of Cases of Disputes over Joint Venture Contracts

Fa (Jing) Fa [1990] No. 27

Pursuant to the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC and other relevant laws and regulations, we hereby provide the following answers to certain questions raised by the people's courts in the trial of cases of disputes over joint venture contracts:

I. Issues Concerning the Acceptance of Cases of Disputes over Joint Venture Contracts

A. Where a party to a joint venture files a lawsuit with a people's court over an economic dispute arising from the performance, modification, or rescission of the joint venture contract, such as disputes over joint venture investment, distribution of profits, liability for breach of contract, assumption of debts, and return of assets, the people's court shall accept the case if the conditions for filing a lawsuit set forth in Article 81 of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation) are satisfied.

B. Where a party to a joint venture files a lawsuit with a people's court over issues concerning the internal management of the joint venture entity, such as the establishment of internal organs and the composition of personnel, the people's court shall not accept the case.

II. Issues Concerning Jurisdiction over Cases of Disputes over Joint Venture Contracts

A. The territorial jurisdiction over cases of disputes over joint venture contracts shall differ according to the different forms of joint venture:

1. Cases of disputes over legal person-type joint venture contracts shall be under the jurisdiction of the people's court of the place where the principal office of the legal person-type joint venture entity is located.

2. Cases of disputes over partnership-type joint venture contracts shall be under the jurisdiction of the people's court of the place where the partnership-type joint venture entity is registered.

3. Cases of disputes over cooperative-type joint venture contracts shall be under the jurisdiction of the people's court of the place where the defendant is located.

B. Where it is truly difficult to place the case under the jurisdiction of the people's court of the place where the principal office of the joint venture entity is located or the place where the joint venture entity is registered, such as when the legal person-type joint venture entity has already completed its cancellation formalities, or the partnership-type joint venture entity that should have gone through registration with the administrative department for industry and commerce has failed to do so, or the joint venture has been dissolved upon expiration of its term, the case may be under the jurisdiction of the people's court of the place where the defendant is located.

III. Issues Concerning the Determination of the Subject Qualification for Joint Venture Contracts

A. The subjects of a joint venture contract shall be enterprise legal persons and institutional legal persons that practice independent accounting and are capable of independently assuming civil liability.

Individual industrial and commercial households, rural contractual operation households, individual partnerships, and private enterprises without legal person status and other economic organizations that enter into a joint venture with an enterprise legal person or an institutional legal person may also become subjects of a joint venture contract.

B. Where a branch of an enterprise legal person or an institutional legal person does not satisfy the conditions for legal person status and, without authorization from the legal person, enters into a joint venture contract in its own name, and such contract is not ratified by the legal person, the contract shall be confirmed as void.

Party and government organs, and institutions that fall under the staffing sequence of party and government organs, military organs, trade unions, the Communist Youth League, women's federations, federations of literary and art circles, associations for science and technology, and various associations, societies, and democratic parties shall not become subjects of a joint venture contract.

IV. Issues Concerning the Guaranteed Minimum Return Clause in Joint Venture Contracts

A. The guaranteed minimum return clause in a joint venture contract usually refers to a clause whereby one party to the joint venture, although investing in the joint venture entity, participating in the joint operation, and sharing the profits of the joint venture, does not bear the liability for losses of the joint venture, and may still recover its capital contribution and receive fixed profits even when the joint venture entity suffers losses. The guaranteed minimum return clause violates the principle of sharing profits and losses and sharing risks that should be followed in joint venture activities, and impairs the legitimate rights and interests of other parties to the joint venture and the creditors of the joint venture entity. Therefore, it shall be confirmed as void. If the joint venture enterprise incurs losses, the fixed profits collected by a party to the joint venture under the guaranteed minimum return clause shall be returned in full to compensate for the losses of the joint venture. If there are no losses, or if there is a surplus after compensation, the remaining part may be treated as profits of the joint venture and shall be reasonably distributed as renegotiated by the parties or redistributed according to the ratio of capital contributions of the parties to the joint venture.

B. Where an enterprise legal person or an institutional legal person, as a party to the joint venture, invests in the joint venture entity but does not participate in the joint operation, nor bears the risk liability of the joint venture, and recovers the principal and interest on schedule regardless of profit or loss, or collects fixed profits on schedule, this constitutes a disguised loan in the form of a joint venture, violating relevant financial regulations, and the contract shall be confirmed as void. In addition to the principal being returnable, any interest that the investing party has already obtained or has agreed to obtain shall be confiscated, and the other party shall be fined an amount equivalent to bank interest.

C. Where a financial trust and investment institution, as a party to a joint venture, invests in the joint venture entity in accordance with the law, it may share fixed profits as agreed in the contract, but shall also bear the liability for losses of the joint venture.

V. Issues Concerning the Withdrawal from a Joint Venture During Its Term

A. Where one or several parties that formed a legal person-type or partnership-type joint venture entity withdraw from the joint venture midway during the term of the joint venture, if the joint venture entity is not dissolved as a result, the property contributed by the withdrawing party as capital shall be returned. If the original property still exists, it shall be returned; if the original property no longer exists or if return is genuinely difficult, compensation shall be made at a depreciated value. The withdrawing party shall share in the profits earned and the debts incurred by the joint venture prior to the withdrawal according to the provisions of the joint venture contract or the ratio of capital contributions. In the case of a partnership-type joint venture entity, the withdrawing party shall also bear joint and several liability for all debts of the joint venture incurred prior to the withdrawal. If the joint venture entity cannot continue to exist due to the midterm withdrawal of one or several parties, the joint venture contract may be rescinded, and the property and debts of the joint venture shall be disposed of accordingly.

B. Where a party withdraws from the joint venture midway under conditions that do not comply with legal provisions or the contract agreement, the withdrawing party shall compensate the joint venture entity for the actual economic losses thus caused. However, if the other parties to the joint venture are also at fault, each party shall bear corresponding economic liability according to the degree of its fault.

VI. Issues Concerning the Calculation of Liquidated Damages and Compensation for Losses under Joint Venture Contracts

Pursuant to the provisions of Article 112(2) of the General Principles of the Civil Law, where the joint venture contract specifies the amount or proportion of liquidated damages, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the contract. If the specified amount or proportion of liquidated damages is excessively high, the people's court may make a reduction based on the actual economic losses; if the specified liquidated damages are insufficient to compensate for the actual economic losses, the shortfall may be made up by compensation for losses. Where the joint venture contract specifies the method for calculating compensation for losses, the amount of compensation for losses to be paid by the party at fault shall be calculated according to the agreed method and the actual circumstances. Where the joint venture contract neither specifies the amount or proportion of liquidated damages nor the method for calculating compensation for losses, the party at fault shall compensate for the actual economic losses.

VII. Issues Concerning the Disposal of Property After the Rescission of a Joint Venture Contract

A. If the joint venture entity is an enterprise legal person, the joint venture entity shall terminate upon rescission of the joint venture contract. After the property of the joint venture is liquidated and debts are paid off, any remaining property shall be distributed according to the agreement or the ratio of capital contributions of the parties to the joint venture.

If the joint venture entity is a partnership-type organization, after the joint venture contract is rescinded and the property of the joint venture is liquidated and debts are paid off, any remaining property shall be used to return capital contributions and distribute profits according to the ratio for profit distribution agreed in the joint venture contract. If the joint venture contract does not specify such ratio and the parties fail to reach an agreement through consultation, the distribution shall be made according to the ratio of capital contributions.

B. When returning joint venture investments, for fixed assets such as equipment and buildings originally contributed by the parties to the joint venture, if the original property still exists, it shall be returned; if the original property no longer exists or if return is genuinely difficult, compensation shall be made at a valued price.

C. For fixed assets such as buildings and equipment purchased by the joint venture entity during the term of the joint venture that cannot be divided, they may be sold at a valued price and the proceeds distributed. Upon sale, the parties to the joint venture shall have a preemptive right.

D. The ownership of trademark rights and patent rights obtained by the joint venture entity during the term of the joint venture after the rescission of the joint venture contract, and the economic compensation related to such ownership, shall be dealt with in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Trademark Law of the PRC and the Patent Law of the PRC. The trademark rights shall be enjoyed by one party to the joint venture. The patent rights may be enjoyed by one party or jointly by all parties to the joint venture. Where one party alone enjoys the trademark rights or patent rights, it shall give appropriate economic compensation to the other parties to the joint venture.

VIII. Issues Concerning the Disposal of Income from Void Joint Ventures

After a joint venture contract is confirmed as void, the income of the joint venture entity during the period of performance of the joint venture contract shall first be used to pay off the debts of the joint venture and to compensate the party without fault for the economic losses suffered due to the invalidity of the contract.

Where the parties maliciously collude to harm the state interest, the collective interest, or the legitimate interests of a third party, or where the joint venture contract becomes void because its content violates the state interest or the social public interest, then, pursuant to the provisions of Article 61(2) and Article 134(3) of the General Principles of the Civil Law, the income of the joint venture entity during the period of performance of the joint venture contract shall be confiscated as illegal income, turned over to the state or the collective, or returned to the third party. In addition, a fine may be imposed on each party to the joint venture; if the conduct constitutes a crime, the matter shall be transferred to the public security or procuratorial authorities for investigation and handling.

IX. Issues Concerning the Assumption of Joint Venture Debts by the Parties to the Joint Venture

A. The liability of the parties to a joint venture for the debts of the joint venture shall be determined differently according to the different forms of joint venture:

1. Where the joint venture entity is an enterprise legal person, it shall assume civil liability with all of its property. The liability of the parties to the joint venture for the joint venture entity shall be limited to the amount of capital contribution each has subscribed. If a party withdraws its subscribed capital contribution to evade debts, the people's court shall, in addition to ordering the withdrawing party to return the full amount, also impose a fine on the responsible person.

2. Where the joint venture entity is a partnership-type organization, the property of the joint venture entity may first be used to pay off the debts of the joint venture. If the property of the joint venture entity is insufficient to satisfy the debts, the parties to the joint venture shall assume civil liability with their own property or the property under their management and operation according to the proportion for bearing debts agreed in the joint venture contract; if the contract does not specify such proportion and the parties fail to reach an agreement through consultation, the liability to be borne by each party shall be determined according to the ratio of capital contributions or the ratio for profit distribution.

The parties to a partnership-type joint venture shall bear joint and several liability for the debts of the joint venture in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and regulations or the agreement of the contract.

3. Where the joint venture is of a cooperative type, the parties to the joint venture shall assume civil liability with their own property or the property under their management and operation respectively, in accordance with the agreement of the contract.

B. Where a rural collective economic organization participates in a partnership-type joint venture by providing its own land use rights, it shall bear the debts of the joint venture in accordance with the agreement of the joint venture contract; if the contract does not specify a proportion for bearing debts, it may bear debts by reference to the ratio of capital contributions or the ratio for profit distribution.

C. Where a party to a joint venture invests by providing the right to use technology as a capital contribution in a partnership-type joint venture, it shall bear the debts of the joint venture in accordance with the agreement of the joint venture contract; if its own property or the property under its management and operation is insufficient to pay off the debts of the joint venture, it may compensate the debts by valuing the right to use the technology for a certain period.

November 12, 1990
